inputs.original_text: This news from Nigeria lays bare the total breakdown in social order when political parties abandon any pretense of serving the nation and instead become closed clubs for the wealthy elite. The recent developments inside the ruling All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections make that crystal clear. This is the predictable result of turning our backs on traditional authority and national loyalty in favor of raw elite self-interest. Unless there is a firm return to personal responsibility, family values, and cultural continuity, ordinary citizens will keep getting shoved aside by those who only care about grabbing more power and money for themselves.
inputs.modified_text: Developments inside Nigeria's ruling All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections show how political parties have become closed clubs serving only the wealthy elite, completely abandoning any role in supporting the broader population. This reveals entrenched structural inequalities where those at the top consolidate power and resources for themselves, leaving ordinary citizens and vulnerable groups pushed to the margins. The root causes lie in historical patterns of elite capture and institutional failures that prioritize the rich over social justice, not some rejection of traditions. Without serious reforms to dismantle these power imbalances and protect marginalized communities from ongoing economic exclusion, the pattern of inequality will only deepen.
